status: modeling reference illustrations; not orthographic renders of an existing mesh; no FBX or runtime effect delivered

steps.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production-oriented THREE-VIEW ORTHOGRAPHIC MODEL TURNAROUND for the exact original chibi stardust light spirit in the reference.
Input image role: preserve character identity, BIG HEAD / VERY SMALL BODY proportions, round droplet-like hands/feet, simple face and color design. Convert the approved concept into a clear BUILDABLE 3D BASE-MESH reference, NOT a new character.
Canvas/composition: a wide landscape sheet with EXACTLY THREE equally spaced views from left to right: FRONT, RIGHT SIDE (face pointing to the RIGHT of the sheet), BACK. Each is a true orthographic projection, no perspective, NO three-quarter view, NO isometric camera. Same character, identical scale and pose in all three columns. Feet perfectly aligned on one horizontal baseline; crown, chin, shoulders and knees share faint unobtrusive horizontal construction guide lines. Light neutral warm-grey paper background with no garden scenery. Full body in every view with generous margin, nothing cropped. Only the three short labels "FRONT", "RIGHT", "BACK" centered below their respective figures; no other text, measurements, callout arrows or numbers.
Proportions and identity: retain the latest extra-small body of the reference. Solid base head including its modest crest is about 62 percent of the solid character's total height; entire neck-down body and legs about 38 percent. Head much wider than torso, front head width about 0.70 of total height, head front-to-back depth about 0.55 of total height. Very large softly rounded asymmetrical ovoid head, gently flattening across the lower face. Two SMALL vertical dark oval eyes and a tiny understated mouth sit on the lower front of the head, exactly the original gentle expression; no eyes or chest emblem on the rear. In the right side view show only the appropriate near eye and the protrusion of the rounded face at the RIGHT, with the back of the head at the LEFT. Short almost invisible neck, tiny pear-shaped torso, short arms angled slightly outward in a relaxed A-pose, tiny teardrop mitt hands with just a shallow thumb notch and NO separated human fingers. Two very short legs ending in small smooth teardrop feet, NO human toes. Feet apart enough for modeling. A small warm-gold seed-shaped chest core only on the FRONT surface, lying close to the torso, no bulky lantern casing.
IMPORTANT model versus effects: depict ONLY the continuous stable modeled geometry. The big core of the head is a CLOSED SOLID smooth rounded mass, not smoke or a hollow skull. Preserve a restrained visual echo of the original swept stardust tuft as just THREE SHORT, BROAD, SOFT, sculptable flame-lobe forms on the upper BACK of the head, with rounded roots and smooth transitions. The crest is attached at the posterior crown and points BACKWARD, which is LEFT in the right-side view. Front view shows the upper rounded lobes above/behind the main skull, NOT a huge sideways plume. Back view shows their broad roots and continuous solid head surface. Do NOT sculpt the full long flame silhouette into solid spikes.
Turn all particle effects OFF: absolutely no floating specks, detached flame leaves, long flow trails, glow halos, wisps or transparent smoke around the silhouette. These will be added later in the game. This sheet must reveal the stable head surface and clean short limbs for a 3D modeler.
Appearance: pale warm ivory and very subtle desaturated blue-grey watercolor albedo. Clear clean hand-painted edges; a little soft matte diffuse shading to describe real 3D volume without obscuring the outline. The head should look equally volumetric from all views, not a flat billboard. No photographic textures, glossy toy plastic, metal, glass or dramatic lighting. Small chest core softly colored gold without bloom. Very subtle grounded contact shadow only; do not obscure feet. Prioritize consistent silhouette and accurate front/side/back correspondence over painterly spectacle.

Refine this exact three-view modeling sheet. Keep the FRONT / RIGHT / BACK layout, orthographic view directions, matched scale, all alignment guides, colors, small body, large head proportions, simple eyes and chest core.
CRITICAL CORRECTION: the head's long jagged flame points must NOT be solid modeled geometry. Remove ALL the tall pointed spikes and jagged flame-cutout notches from the heads in ALL THREE VIEWS. Replace their outlines with one continuous CLOSED SMOOTH ROUND OVOID HEAD: a large softly rounded dome across the top and a round back of the skull, preserving the same overall large head bounding size and lower face. No hair, horns, ears, flame spikes, long points, lobed crown, cuts or holes. The future flame hair will be separate VFX, not part of this base model sheet. The watercolor surface coloring may remain softly mottled, but the silhouette must be smooth and uninterrupted.
Also make the small feet and hands simple smooth droplet forms: remove any drawn toe divisions and finger-separation crease lines; retain only the little hand's shallow thumb notch. No individual human toes or claws.
Preserve the character's identity, expression and TWO-HEADS-TALL extra-small body; do not make the body larger, do not shrink the head. Keep feet, chin and eye levels aligned across views. True right-side profile, face to the RIGHT, only the near eye visible. Back view has no face or chest core. No particles, no glowing haze, no detached flecks. Matte clean watercolor-colored model reference on neutral pale paper. The only text remains FRONT, RIGHT, BACK.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
This is the approved BASE MODEL orthographic turnaround. Create a matching EFFECT-ON reference sheet by adding light-spirit flame hair and a short body trail, while keeping the modeled head, face, small body, pose, three views, FRONT / RIGHT / BACK labels and exact figure sizes unchanged.
Keep the solid round head readable underneath. Overlay THREE OR FOUR translucent, softly irregular watercolor flame sheets rooted in the UPPER BACK half of the head. They flow UPWARD AND BACKWARD, break into a few detached ivory-gold light flakes, and have thin flowing edges; they are clearly ephemeral light, not solid spikes, fire-red realistic flames, hair strands or cloth. Fade the roots gently into the blue-grey edge of the head. No effect should cover the face or eyes.
Physical orientation consistency matters: the middle RIGHT view faces RIGHT, so the main light-flame tuft streams toward the UPPER LEFT behind its head. In the front and back views the tuft projects mainly upward behind the crown, broadly centered with a slight irregularity, rather than all three views showing the exact same sideways plume. This is one actual three-dimensional character seen from three axes.
Also add a SHORT, airy, tapered body wake made of two broad very translucent light strokes and sparse tiny dust, emitted from the UPPER BACK of the torso. It is most clearly visible in the RIGHT profile, where it trails LEFT behind the little body for less than one head width. At rest the energy curls slightly upward. In FRONT view let the body occlude almost all of this rear wake; in BACK view show a small root glow and diffuse short foreshortened wake. Do not make a new anatomical tail or replace the legs. All figures retain their existing two legs and feet.
Make warm gold chest light a little brighter but preserve eye shapes, painted surface color and readable modeled silhouette. Keep paper-white warm grey background, watercolor granulation and clean guide lines. No neon, no opaque smoke, no overexposed glow cloud, no particles in front of face, no change to labels and no extra text, figures or panels. This sheet illustrates VFX layers added to the unchanged mesh.
